Subject: POC demo recap + initial shortlist + artifacts (prompt pack & benchmarks)

Alex / Priya —

Great meeting yesterday, thanks for the thoughtful questions. I pulled together an initial recommended shortlist and the artifacts you asked for. Summary below, attached are the prompt pack and the raw benchmark CSVs: novanet_prompt_pack_v1.zip and benchmarks_novanet_latency_cost.csv.

High-level findings (short):
- Shortlist: tiny-llama-7b-q4 (fast+cheap), opt-13b-compat (balanced quality, mid cost), redwood-rlm-25b-slim (best quality, higher cost).
- For 10 RPS and typical query lengths (~40 tokens average response), tiny-llama-7b-q4 yields ~60–80ms p95 inference on P4d reserved pools with our continuous batching disabled for single-tenant low-latency mode. opt-13b-compat lands ~120–160ms p95, redwood-rlm-25b-slim ~220–280ms p95. See CSV for test harness details.
- With prefix/KV caching enabled for common query prefixes, the effective token billing drops ~15–30% depending on pattern reuse; request-level amortization matters — we call this out in the benchmarks.

Why this shortlist: practical tradeoffs we think map to NovaNet’s asks
- tiny-llama-7b-q4: lowest unit cost and best tail latency at the expense of some long-form factuality losses. Good for search re-ranking and short-answer widgets.
- opt-13b-compat: middle ground — better retained instruction-following than tiny-llama, reasonable latency/cost for most traffic shapes.
- redwood-rlm-25b-slim: best for complex summarization or synthesis tasks where hallucination tolerance is low; expect higher latency and cost but fewer quality regressions.

Quality regression concerns
- We observed that tiny-llama-7b-q4 degrades on multi-step extraction prompts in our internal evals; we included a prompt subset (in the pack) labeled 'extraction_stress' that reproduced the issue. If you need extraction-heavy routes, we recommend either opt-13b-compat with tuned prompt templates or redwood-rlm-25b-slim for the highest-fidelity.

Next suggested steps (recommended cadence):
1) Infra/Eng: run the CSV through your perf team and flag any outlier latencies (we used p95 across 5000 queries).
2) Product/ML: try the provided prompt_pack in a shadow pass for 48 hours against real queries, capture metrics (relevance, latency, failure modes).
3) Commercial: if opt-13b-compat looks like the sweet spot, we can scope a short reserved test (14-day dedicated slice) to validate cost and SLA.

I linked the HubSpot deal above and added the SOW draft for early guardrails. Let us know which route you want to prioritize and we'll schedule a follow-up technical runbook.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Priya / Alex —

Quick answers and actions below; copying Marissa and Ben for commercial + product ops follow-up.

1) Harness config: attached CSV includes an extra worksheet with harness params (batch_size=1 for low-latency tests; beam=1; seq_len distribution: req tokens=20±10, resp tokens=40±15; concurrency simulated as steady 10 RPS). I also uploaded a short README to the drive link: https://redwood-internal.drive/nn/poc/benchmarks (see harness_README.md). If you want the JMeter/Locust script we used, we can share it.

2) PII / prompt pack: the prompt_pack_v1 uses synthetic replacements for any customer-identifying tokens; lines labeled 'real-data-only' are redacted. For shadow testing we recommend enabling token masking at the client side (we can provide a small sanitization script in the next pack).

3) Reserved slice logging: for a 14-day dedicated test we provide request-level traces, per-token billing breakdowns, and optional audit export (S3-compatible) for all requests — standard in Redwood Dedicated trials. Marissa will follow up with a sample retention policy and Ben will outline a proposed pricing guardrail.
